greet.text: Ah, an audience! Pip Fairweather, teller of tales, singer of songs, occasional washer of tankards.

options.text: A halfling, playing the lute? Wren likes you already.

song.text:
[i]Oh the lantern burns where the river bends,
and it burned before the hills began,
and it waits for one whose journey ends
where the light outlasts the man...[/i]

An old tune. Nobody knows who wrote it.

rumour.text: They say there's a lantern hidden in these hills that has never once gone out. Shepherds swear they've seen its light on the ridge on moonless nights. Folk who go looking come back empty-handed, or don't come back.

options.text: Elowen: "That is exactly the lantern I'm looking for."

elowen.text: Is it now? Then I'll write a song about you, miss, whether it ends well or badly. Bad endings sell better, but I'm rooting for you.

wren.text: Takes one to know one. Keep your fingers out of my tip jar, friend, and I'll keep mine out of your pockets.
